## Not a bug — the fast-fail on `blocked` is intended, enforced behaviour

Operator ruling: review-plan fast-failing on a blocked ticket is **intended**, not a defect.

Cited authority, `AGENTS.md:128-131`:

> This is partly **enforced**: `review-plan` on a ticket that is not yet claimable — status
> `closed`/`idea`/`blocked`, or `open` but still blocked by an unclosed dependency —
> **fast-fails with no LLM** (unsigned `INDETERMINATE`, exit 2) unless you pass `--force`;
> close the prerequisites, then review.

And the rationale it enforces, `AGENTS.md:123-127`:

> **Plan-review in dependency order — never review a ticket and its dependencies in parallel.**
> A review pins its direct dependencies' (children/prerequisites') material, so a dependency
> changing after the review invalidates it.

So the refusal is the mechanism working: reviewing a blocked ticket would certify a plan against
material its unclosed blockers can still change, producing an attestation that is stale on arrival.
`--force` is the documented lever, deliberately reserved for an operator's judgement call rather
than routine use.

### The premise this ticket rests on

It argues the refusal's premise 'is now false' because a sibling change widened `claim` to accept a
`blocked` source status. That inverts the dependency: **the documented design is the fixed point,
and a change that collides with it is the thing to re-examine** — not the other way round.

Whether `claim` should accept `blocked` at all is a live question I have referred back to the agent
that made that change, since the two behaviours have to agree and the review-plan side is settled.
Resolving it there is the right place; it is not resolved by relaxing an enforced invariant here.

### What survives

Nothing that warrants code change under this ticket. If a gated `task`/`story`/`epic` genuinely
needs to refresh an attestation while blocked, the sanctioned answer per AGENTS.md is to **close the
prerequisites first** — which is also what makes the resulting attestation meaningful.

Closing `not_a_bug`. Filed in good faith off a real observation; the observation is just a
consequence of the design rather than a violation of it.
